as_told.title: Huge red square hovers over Vandenberg launch facility

tellings.quote: The incursions began on October 14th, 2003 when Boeing contractors reported a massive glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites.
tellings.difference: Gives the date as October 14, 2003, says it was red, glowing and silent over two missile defence sites, says Boeing contractors reported it, and cites Air Force records, AARO and the FBI.
tellings.link_reason: A large glowing rectangular or square object at Vandenberg in 2003, matching Shurmer's football-sized rectangle; the five-incident story is a broader series.

plain: On October 14, 2003, a huge red square is said to have come in from the ocean and hovered over Vandenberg Air Force Base in California, as reported by workers for the aircraft maker Boeing. Ryan Graves, a former Navy fighter pilot, tells it from the contractors' account. He describes "a very large 100yard sided, uh, red square" that came from the sea and hung low over one of the launch sites. Jeff Natelli, who says he responded to events at the base, describes "a massive glowing red square silently hovering over two missile defense sites." He says the case is backed by Air Force records and mentions a member of Congress, Representative Luna, along with AARO, the Pentagon's current UFO office, and the FBI. Michael Shermer, a well-known skeptic, refers to it during a debate as the one "off the coast" that was "rectangular like football size." If true, a large unknown object sat over sensitive missile sites.
